definitions.short: properly, redundant ; hence, over and above , as adjective, noun, adverb or conjunction
definitions.full: H3148. yother יֹתֵר יוֺתֵר, noun masculine superiority, advantage, excess (late) (properly Qal participle of יתר ) — absolute יוֺתֵר Eccl 7:16 2 t.; יֹתֵר 2:15 4 t.; — superiority, advantage מִןהַֿכְּסִיל לֶחָכָם מַהיּֿוֺתֵר 6:8 what advantage hath the wise over the fool ? probably also מֵהֵמָּה יֹתֵר 12:12 (as to) what is more than these (see VB); absolute לָאָדָם מַהיֹּֿתֵר 6:11 ; הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ לְרֹאֵי יֹתֵר 7:11 ; elsewhere adverb to excess, overmuch 2:15 ; 7:16 ; followed by מִן (as often in Late Hebrew), מִמֶּנִּי יוֺתֵר Est 6:6 more than me ; שֶׁ ׳יֹתֵר = besides that Eccl 12:9 .

occurrences.englishText: So Haman came in. The king said to him, “What shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor?”
Then I said in my heart, “As it happens to the fool, so will it happen even to me; and why was I then more wise?” Then I said in my heart that this also is vanity.
For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knows how to walk before the living?
For there are many words that create vanity. What does that profit man?
Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those who see the sun.
Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself?
Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.
